clue.text: Film director's family felt the heat at first

blocks.note: fried = felt the heat, as food in a pan

explanation.surface: A director's relatives wilt under pressure, or in a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written back to front: 'family' is read first but goes second. William Friedkin directed The Exorcist and The French Connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Friedkin, who made The Exorcist and The French Connection, is one film director, named only by his job.

clue.text: Poorly insured son is going bankrupt

indicators.note: the letters are in bad shape, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: An ill man learns his insurance won't stop the family business going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is going' reads like part of 'going bankrupt' but it belongs with 'son': S departs. 'Bankrupt' as an adjective matches RUINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the financial sense: a ruined firm has lost everything, which is what bankrupt means.

clue.text: New exotic pen in special case

indicators.note: the letters are made new, into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fancy new fountain pen sits in its presentation box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like the box the pen comes in; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrase names something the usual rule does not apply to.

clue.text: They swim off across river

blocks.note: to off someone is to kill them

explanation.surface: Swimmers push away from the bank and head across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as swimming away; it is the slang verb for murder. The definition is a bare description: krill swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny crustaceans that swim in vast ocean swarms.

clue.text: Most impressive split headline is French

blocks.note: split into head (NOB, slang for head) and line (L)

explanation.surface: A newspaper splits a headline in two and prints it in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headline' looks like one word of journalism but is two: NOB for head, L for line. 'Nob' is old British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: noble means grand or stately, and the superlative ending matches 'Most'.

clue.text: Nutcases operated in Langley?

blocks.note: the CIA's headquarters is at Langley, Virginia

explanation.surface: Madmen were running things at CIA headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutcases' reads as lunatics; split it as nut-cases, and a skull is the case for the head, slang 'nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crania, skulls, are the cases that hold the 'nut', or head.

clue.text: Italian composer has a revolutionary massage in India

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the crossword's stock revolutionary
I = India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An Italian composer on tour treats himself to a rebel-style massage in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In India' looks like a location but gives two pieces, IN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and church music.

clue.text: Everyone around the Bluegrass state is radical

blocks.note: KY = Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State

explanation.surface: Everybody in Kentucky has extreme politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is political on the surface but chemical in the answer: an alkyl is a radical, a group of atoms, such as methyl.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an alkyl group, such as methyl, is called a radical.

clue.text: Dinner set occasionally given to act as compensation

indicators.note: take only some letters, every other one

blocks.note: a turn = an act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A dinner service is handed over now and then to pay someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters stop at E; the final T of 'set' is left out. 'Turn' is a stage act, as in a comedian doing a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given in return is given as compensation.

clue.text: Wave after round trip

blocks.note: a circuit = a round, as of a track
a breaker is a large wave

explanation.surface: A wave of illness follows a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round trip' is a false phrase: 'round' is wordplay and 'trip' alone is the definition. A circuit breaker is the switch that trips when a circuit overloads.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit breaker is also called a trip switch, since it trips to cut the power.

clue.text: Writer attached to China as correspondent

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, the thing you write with
rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so china = pal

explanation.surface: A writer is posted to China as a foreign correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone you correspond with by letter.

clue.text: English characteristic that the elitists might not like?

definitions.text: that the elitists might not like?

explanation.surface: A national trait that snobs would disapprove of.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description rather than a synonym, hence the question mark: elitists prefer hierarchy to equality.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitists believe some people are better than others, so equality is what they would dislike.

clue.text: Some fritter billions, 8 for Da Ponte's works?

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the words
8 down is IN RETURN, so the letters come back the other way

explanation.surface: Someone squanders billions in exchange for Da Ponte's operas.
explanation.walkthrough: '8 for' borrows the answer to 8 down, IN RETURN, as a reversal signal. Lorenzo Da Ponte wrote the words for Mozart's Figaro, Don Giovanni and Così.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Ponte was a librettist, so his works are libretti, the texts of operas.

clue.text: People who sell Dior's latest and earliest fashions

indicators.note: as a verb: shapes the letters into something new

explanation.surface: Shops that sell both the newest and the earliest Dior collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a noun in a Dior clue; it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: shopkeepers selling goods to the public rather than to the trade.

clue.text: Unelected Head of State visits a European port

indicators.note: to visit is to go into someone's place

blocks.note: CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A king makes a state visit to a European harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A European port' reads as one phrase, but Acre is in Israel: 'port' alone is the definition. CR is King Charles's cipher, as ER was the Queen's.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient port on the coast of northern Israel.

clue.text: American carved a large breast in white stone

indicators.note: the letters are cut into a new shape

explanation.surface: An American sculptor carves a big bust out of white marble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carved' fits the stone so well it passes for description; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft, fine-grained white stone used for carving.

clue.text: Jack the Ripper copycat taking pee? He sprays all over the place

definitions.text: He sprays all over the place

blocks.note: a slasher is a knife-wielding attacker
the letter P, as it sounds

explanation.surface: A copycat killer turns out to be merely someone urinating everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pee' is the spoken name of the letter P, not a bodily function, though the surface wants it to be both.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful coinage: the -ER ending makes a person out of the verb splash, and the definition describes that messy habit.

clue.text: Start working after drinking a short

indicators.note: PER is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: a = per (as in 'twice a day'), cut short to PE

explanation.surface: Someone starts the working day after knocking back a short, a small strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A short' looks like a whisky; 'a' means per, as in fifty miles an hour, and 'short' clips it to PE. 'After' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you open a meeting or a debate when you begin it.

clue.text: Island king into heavy metal and current pop

explanation.surface: An island king gets into heavy metal and modern pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all music, heavy metal and current pop, but each word is chemistry, physics or family.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Loosely, it means 10s?

indicators.note: the letters are taken loosely, not in order

explanation.surface: A dictionary shrugs that the word roughly means tens.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is PEN PAL, so '10s' are pen pals: read cryptically, mates in the pen (prison), which is what inmates are.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are prison pals, mates in the pen, a jokey reading of pen pals.

clue.text: Doctor's striking costume

blocks.note: to doctor = to rig, tamper with

explanation.surface: A doctor wears an eye-catching outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb and 'striking' means on strike, not eye-catching. 'Rig-out' is British for an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a complete outfit, which makes costume a close synonym.

clue.text: Circulated document provided one better political stance

indicators.note: sent round, so the whole string turns back

explanation.surface: A memo is sent round proposing a better political line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulated' reads as sending a memo round the office; it reverses everything after it. 'Better' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: opposing all war is one political position a person may take.

clue.text: Home Office supports regular uprising

blocks.note: a GI is a regular soldier
'the offices' is an old euphemism for the lavatory

explanation.surface: The Home Office backs a routine rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home Office' is the British interior ministry, but the words split: 'Home' is the definition and 'Office' the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a home built of snow blocks.

clue.text: One rarely scores work at the start of a romance

blocks.note: to romance is to invent stories, so a romance is a lie

explanation.surface: A lothario rarely succeeds when he's working at the beginning of an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' is sexual in the surface but footballing in the definition: goalkeepers seldom score goals.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalie is a goalkeeper, a player who rarely scores.

clue.text: Despair for one pair of soldiers

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
a soldier ant, one of the colony's defenders

explanation.surface: Someone gives up hope over a couple of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Giant Despair is the giant of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, so Despair is one example of a giant. 'Pair of soldiers' means two different soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Despair is the ogre who imprisons Christian in Doubting Castle.

clue.text: Author in Hanoi's Premier Hotel worked out pi

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer at a Hanoi hotel calculates pi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pi' sits at the end looking like maths; it is the crossword abbreviation for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi, short for pious, describes someone sanctimonious, holier-than-thou.

clue.text: Bears seen in British castles

blocks.note: in chess the castle is the rook

explanation.surface: Bears have been spotted living in British castles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' is a verb, to tolerate; the animals are a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook is to bear or tolerate, as in 'brooks no argument'.

clue.text: Planet virtually consumed in swamp

indicators.note: almost all of it: the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A whole planet has been swallowed by a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' reads as a bog but it is a verb, to flood or drench.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to flood or drench something, soaking it completely.
